args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. v2.3.1 (and its staging candidate v2.3.1-rc) were unhealthy. Rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west and eu-west), and it's now passing health checks. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in all three regions, failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback version:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production.
- **Result:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, and the error rate has dropped to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** It explains the failed release, the rollback and the result. It also includes a follow-up to find the root cause before v2.3.1 is deployed again. Its test build (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging, so the problem was visible before the production deploy.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
